status: Specified after inspecting the first two-dataset benchmark, before running this expanded experiment; not externally preregistered.
question: When does monotone probability recalibration change capacity-constrained screening decisions, and do calibration-selection criteria transfer under temporal shift and missing data?
fit_replicate_definition: Original training/calibration sample plus two independent bootstrap perturbations; temporal data use circular blocks of 100 rows; no test records are resampled for fitting.
tuning: Three prespecified candidates per machine-learning model, chosen by Brier loss on an inner training-only holdout. Hyperparameter tuning is repeated for every fitting replicate.
calibration: Disjoint calibration-fit and calibration-selection blocks; identity, monotone logit-Platt, monotone beta, isotonic.
stress: Clean; independent cell missingness and whole-record predictor outage at rates 0.15, 0.30, 0.50; three paired mask replicates. No labels are altered.
inference: Paired 2000-draw test bootstrap conditional on the original fitted models and actions; temporal blocks of 100, with 25/250 sensitivity. Three fitting replicates are reported separately as a stability range, not a confidence interval.
business_interpretation: Observed-label screening utility with assumed unit reward and common cost. No causal treatment effect, realized revenue, organizational readiness, or strategic decision-quality effect is estimated.
tie_rule: All monotone calibration policies preserve raw-score order, then original record ID. Isotonic plateau ties do not reorder cases.
